## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- This break has no listed tide preference to compare the sources with.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- Limited information is available about this break's best season.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Seven readable sources from seven publishers; all are community, forecast-site or magazine grade. No guidebook text could be checked, and no official or peer-reviewed source exists for the break. WIND: four sources name the best or offshore wind: N (Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, Surfsphere) and NE (Surfing-Waves). N is 45 deg from the profile NE (45), at the edge of tolerance. The Stormrider page's embedded break data (script only, not checkable) gives 'Easterly' wind, 3-15 ft, swell 'SW - N', 'Low tide only' and 'uneven reef & sand'. Its description says it only breaks in big swells at low tide. SWELL DIRECTION: WNW (Surf-Forecast), NW (Surfing-Waves, Yeeew) and W (Tidal Trip), all inside the profile window 270-340. SIZE: WannaSurf 6-8 ft to 16 ft+ and Surfing-Waves 'big swells, holds 12ft+'. Several sources say it needs big swell, so the profile minimum of 4 ft may be low. The Stormrider script data gives a 3 ft minimum. TIDE: low tide is consistent across WannaSurf, World Beach Guide, Surfsphere, Tidal Trip (and the Stormrider script data). The profile has tide null, so this could not be compared; consider setting tide_preference to low. PERIOD: no source gives a swell period. Surf-Forecast only says it gets a mix of groundswells and windswells. SEASON: Yeeew gives October-March, consistent with the profile's November-March; Surf-Forecast says summer is flat. WannaSurf's 'Good swell direction' field is empty on the page. The earlier note about a second WannaSurf page listing S/NE swell was not re-checked (no URL in the evidence). No page gives a content date except Surfsphere (2023).

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 6–8 ft (2–2.5 m) | documented | S2, S3, S4 | `wave_height_min_ft` 4 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | big swells (triple overhead) · surfer heights (face) | documented | S7 | no separate setting; working range 4–15 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 16 ft (5 m) or more | documented | S2, S3 | `wave_height_max_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 2-2.5 m / 6-8 ft (its own conversion; face or offshore height not stated), and Surfing-Waves and World Beach Guide say it needs big swells or plenty of swell.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Starts working at 2m-2.5m / 6ft-8ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
  - S3 (Surfing-Waves.com): “A point break that starts breaking in big swells and can hold 12ft+.”
  - S4 (World Beach Guide): “Epic when it's on but relatively inconsistent requiring plenty of swell and a low tide”
- **Ideal range**: Tidal Trip says Safi is best when there are big swells (triple overhead), a face height relative to the surfer with no number in feet.
  - S7 (Tidal Trip): “Safi is the best wave to surf when there are BIG swells (triple overhead).”
- **Maximum suitable**: WannaSurf says it holds up to 5 m / 16 ft and over and Surfing-Waves that it can hold 12 ft+; both bounds are open-ended and no source gives a size at which it stops working.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Starts working at 2m-2.5m / 6ft-8ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
  - S3 (Surfing-Waves.com): “A point break that starts breaking in big swells and can hold 12ft+.”

### Swell direction

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ideal bearing | 270–315° (W to NW, clockwise) | documented | S1, S3, S6, S7 | `optimal_swell_direction` 290–320° (WNW to NW, clockwise) |
| Acceptable range | — | not documented | — | `swell_window` 270–340° (W to NNW, clockwise) |
| Blocked directions | — | not documented | — | no separate setting (outside `swell_window`) |
| Exposure | exposed point that needs plenty of swell and is relatively inconsistent | documented | S1, S4, S7 | no setting |

Notes:

- **Ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast gives west-northwest as ideal, Surfing-Waves and Yeeew a (solid) northwesterly swell and Tidal Trip W swells, so the named best directions span W to NW.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “the ideal swell direction is from the west northwest”
  - S3 (Surfing-Waves.com): “Once the northwesterly swell starts running this wave can break for up to 500 meters and produces big hollow barrels.”
  - S6 (Yeeew!): “On a solid north-west swell, Safi Point produces some of the best right-hand barrels in the world.”
  - S7 (Tidal Trip): “It is a fickle wave, however when the stars align (W swells and low tide), it might be the best tube in Morocco.”
- **Acceptable range**: No excerpt states a range of working swell directions; the sources name only best directions (W to NW, recorded under ideal_bearing).
- **Blocked directions**: No excerpt names swell directions that are blocked or shadowed by land or reefs.
- **Exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed point break, World Beach Guide says it is relatively inconsistent and needs plenty of swell, and Tidal Trip calls it a fickle wave.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “Safi Garden (Le Jardin) in Central Morocco is an exposed point break.”
  - S4 (World Beach Guide): “Epic when it's on but relatively inconsistent requiring plenty of swell and a low tide”
  - S7 (Tidal Trip): “It is a fickle wave, however when the stars align (W swells and low tide), it might be the best tube in Morocco.”
